## Japan — Imperial Court: The Imperial House and Royal House of Chosen

### The Imperial House — The Reigning Sovereign

**His Imperial Majesty Hirohito** the reigning Emperor of Japan (124th of the line), is the first son of the late Emperor Taisho (Taisho Tenno), born on April 29th, 1901. He was nominated Heir-Apparent on September 9th, 1912, being at the same time appointed Sub-Lieutenant of the Army and Second Sub-Lieutenant of the Imperial Navy and decorated with the Grand Cordon of the Chrysanthemum; promoted to Lieutenant of the Army and 1st Sub-Lieutenant of the Navy on October 31st, 1914; to Captain and Lieutenant on October 31st, 1916; promoted to Major and Lieut.-Commander on Oct. 31st, 1920; visited Europe in 1921; appointed Regent on Nov. 25th, 1921; promoted to Lieut.Colonel and Commander on Oct. 31st, 1923; married Princess Nagako Kuni (first daughter of H.I.H. Prince Kuni) on Jan. 26th, 1924; promoted to Colonel and Captain (Navy) on Oct. 31st, 1924; acceded to the Throne on the death of his father Emperor Taisho on Dec. 25th, 1926; formally enthroned on Nov. 10th, 1928. On March 3rd, 1921 His Majesty (then Crown Prince) proceeded to Europe to make observations and exchange courtesies with the sovereigns and rulers of European countries, returning home in September the same year. It was an epoch-making event in the history of the Japanese Imperial House as it was the first Crown Prince of this Empire who ever stepped out of the country and visited foreign lands, and moreover it was an unqualified success in every respect, particularly having had the result of promoting and further cementing the happy relations between Japan and her friendly Powers in the Occident. After returning from the foreign tour, he was appointed Regent in November, 1921, to conduct affairs of State in place of his Imperial father who, on account of chronic illness, was incapacitated from performing his onerous duties as Emperor. In January, 1924, he married Princess Nagako, eldest daughter of H.I.H. General Prince Kuniyoshi Kuni. Then on the 25th of December, 1926, following the death of his father Emperor Yoshihito (Taisho Tenno) he ascended the Throne as the 124th Emperor, the new era named Showa being adopted for his reign. The enthronement of the sovereign was officially celebrated at the ancient Capital of Kyoto in November (10th to 15th), 1928, after the lapse of one year's mourning over the demise of the departed Emperor according to traditional custom, the national function being performed with time-honoured ceremonies. — p. 43 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Nagako** the Empress, first daughter of the late Prince Kuniyoshi Kuni, born on March 6th, 1903. Her Majesty was educated at the Peeresses' School and afterward studied under private tutors at her home. Married the Emperor (then Crown Prince) Jan. 26th, 1924. — p. 43 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Sadako** the Empress Dowager (consort of the late Emperor Taisho), born June 25th, 1884; fourth daughter of the late Prince Michitaka Kujo, a noble of the first rank; married Emperor Taisho (then Crown Prince) on May 10th, 1900; widow Dec. 25th, 1926. — p. 43 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor

**Chichibu-no-Miya** (Residence—Akasaka-ku, Tokyo). — p. 43 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor — Chichibu-no-Miya

**Prince Yasuhito** present head (1st of the line) and second son of the late Emperor Taisho, born June 25th, 1902. His house-name was formerly Atsu-no-Miya, but on attaining majority in June, 1922 the Prince founded a new house (Chichibu-no-Miya) by Imperial order. The Prince was educated at the Peers' School and, after finishing the middle school course of the institution, entered the Central Military Preparatory School in 1917 to receive military education; further studied at the Military Academy, graduating in 1922; appointed Sub-Lieutenant (infantry) October 1922 and attached to Imperial Guards Division; promoted to Lieutenant, 1925; went abroad to study at Oxford, 1925-26; returned in January 1927; married Miss Setsu-ko, daughter of Mr. Tsuneo Matsudaira, then Ambassador to the Court of St. James', 1928; promoted to Captain, 1930; visited Manchoukuo, 1934; promoted to Major, 1935; Lieut.-Col., 1938, attended British Coronation, 1937. The Prince is Honorary President, British Association (Tokyo), Siamese Association (Tokyo), Swedish Association of Japan, Peers' Club. Honorary member, Ski Club of Great Britain, Alpine Ski Club of England. — p. 43 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Setsuko** consort of the above, is daughter of Mr. Tsuneo Matsudaira, Minister of the Imperial Household, and niece of Viscount Yasuo Matsudaira. Was born Sept.9th, 1909; educated at the Peeresses' School and later in the United States; married the Prince Sept. 28th, 1928. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor

**Takamatsu-no-Miya** (Residence—Takanawa Nishidaimachi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo). — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor — Takamatsu-no-Miya

**Prince Nobuhito** present head (1st of the line) and third son of the late Emperor Taisho, born January 3, 1905. Graduated from Peers' School, 1921, from Naval College, 1924; appointed 2nd Sub-Lieutenant, December 1925; 1st Sub-Lieutenant, 1926; meanwhile studied at the Torpedo School, 1925-26; Naval Aviation School at Kasumigaura, 1927; Naval Gunnery School at Yokosuka, 1930-31; promoted to Lieutenant, 1930 and attached to the Naval Staff Board; appointed squadron Commander of the warship Takao, 1932; transferred to the Fuso in similar capacity, 1933; promoted to Lieut.-Commdr., 1935. The Prince married Princess Kikuko, daughter of the late Prince Yoshitaka Tokugawa, February 1930; went abroad the same year to return the courtesy of the British Court accompanied by the Princess. The Prince is Honorary President, the Japan Fine Arts Association, the Turco-Japanese Society and the Japan-Denmark Society, both of Tokyo. The Prince was formerly called Teru-no-Miya, but in July, 1931, he set up a new house and assumed the family-name, Takamatsu-no-Miya. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Kikuko** consort of the above, is sister of Prince Yoshimitsu Tokugawa and was born Dec. 26th, 1911. Married the Prince Feb. 4th, 1930. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor

### The Imperial House — Brothers of the Emperor — Mikasa-no-Miya

**Prince Takahito** present head (1st of the line) and fourth son of late Emperor Taisho and the youngest brother of the reigning Emperor, born Dec. 2nd, 1915. The Prince finished the middle school course of the Peers' School in 1932; the Military Academy in June, 1936; is attached to the 15th Regiment (Cavalry) as Cadet. On attaining his majority in 1935, the Prince was granted the name of Mikasa and founded a new house. Promoted to Sub-Lieut. 1936, Lieut., 1937. The Prince visited Manchoukuo in 1936. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Other Members of the Imperial Family

**Kan-in-no-Miya** (Residence—Nagata-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo). The House was founded by Prince Naohito (1703-52, A.D.), eldest son of Higashiyama Tenno (113th Emperor). — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Other Members of the Imperial Family — Kan-in-no-Miya

**Prince Kotohito** head (6th of the line), Field Marshal, Supreme War Councillor and Chief of General Staff. Is the 16th son of the late Prince Kuniie Fushimi; born Sept. 22nd, 1865; studied at the Military Preparatory Schools and then at the Military Academy; later studied at a French Military School; took part in the Japan-China and the Russo-Japanese Wars; promoted to Lieut.-General in 1905; appointed Commander of the Imperial Guards Division in 1906; promoted to General and made Supreme War Councillor in 1912; Field Marshal in 1919; appointed Chief of General Staff, Dec. 1931. In 1921 the Prince accompanied the Crown Prince (present Emperor) on his tour of Europe. Prince is Hon. President of the Japan Red Cross Society, the Japan Sericultural Association, the Franco-Japanese Society, the Russo-Japanese Society, the Tokyo Geological Society, the Military Club, the Tokyo Club and many other similar bodies. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Chieko** Consort of the above, 2nd daughter of the late Prince Sanetomi Sanjo; born May 25th, 1872. Married the Prince Dec. 19th, 1891. The Princess is Honorary President of the Japan Women's Education Association and of the Japan Red Cross Voluntary Nurses' Association. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Haruhito** 2nd son of Prince Kotohito, born Aug. 3rd, 1902. Studied at the Peers' School and then at the Military Academy; is Captain of Cavalry attached to the Cavalry School as instructor and superintendent of research department, appointed Major of Cavalry, July, 1937. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Naoko** consort of the above, 4th daughter of the late Prince Saneteru Ichijo; born Nov. 7th, 1908; married Prince Haruhito July 14th, 1926. — p. 44 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

The House is the oldest of the princely families, founded in the 14th century by a son of Gohanazono Tenno, the 102nd Emperor. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Other Members of the Imperial Family — Fushimi-no-Miya

**Prince Hiroyasu** present head (23rd of the line) and eldest son of the late General Prince Sadanaru; born Oct. 16th, 1875; succeeded to the House of Prince Kwacho in 1883, but returned to the present House in July 1904; studied at the Naval Academy and then in Germany; took part in the Russo-Japanese War and was wounded on board the Mikasa in the battle of the Yellow Sea (Aug. 1904); studied in England, 1909-10; was in command of the Takachiho, 1910; Vice-Admiral, 1917; full Admiral, 1922; Supreme War Councillor, 1920; appointed Chief of Naval Staff Board, Feb. 1932; Admiral of Fleet, May 1932. The Prince is Hon. President of the Imperial Life Boat Association, the Japan Seamen's Relief Association, the Cancer Research Society, the Naval Club, the Japan-German Society, the Scientific & Chemical Research Institute, etc. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Tsuneko** consort of the above, 9th daughter of the late Prince Keiki Tokugawa (the last Shogun). Born Sept. 23rd, 1882. Married Jan. 9th, 1897. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Hiroyoshi** eldest son of Prince Hiroyasu, born 1897; studied at the Naval Academy; married Princess Tokiko, 3rd daughter of Prince Ichijo, in 1919; is Commander of the Navy; appointed Vice-Commander of the Cruiser Naka, Nov. 1934; Commander of the Mine Layer Itsukushima, Nov. 1935; Commander of 3rd Destroyer Flotilla, 1936. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Tokiko** consort of the above, 3rd daughter of Prince Saneteru Ichijo, born 1902. Married Dec. 23rd, 1919. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**(Prince Hironobu** 3rd son of Prince Hiroyasu, born 1905, created a new House in 1926 by order of the late Emperor Taisho and is now called Marquis Kwacho. He graduated from the Naval Academy in 1925). — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Other Members of the Imperial Family — Yamashina-no-Miya

**Dowager Princess Hisako** mother of Prince Takehiko and consort of the late Prince Kikumaro, 3rd daughter of the late Prince Tadayoshi Shimazu; born Feb. 7th, 1874; widow, 1908. Prince Takehiko has four brothers, Prince Yoshimaro (born 1901), Prince Fujimaro (born 1905), Prince Hagimaro (born 1906) and Prince Shigemaro (born 1908), who were all ordered to set up new houses and are now known as Marquis Yamashina, Marquis Tsukuba, Count Kashima (died Aug.1932) and Count Katsuragi respectively. They are no longer members of the Imperial Family. — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Takehiko** head (3rd of the line), eldest son of the late Prince Kikumaro; born Feb. 13th, 1898; studied at the Naval Academy; attached to the Naval Aviation Corps as Sub.-Lieutenant and attached to the Naval Staff Board; retired from active service in 1927 on account of declining health; promoted to Lieut.-Commander in 1929 and at the same time placed on waiting list. Married Princess Sakiko, 2nd daughter of the late Prince Kuniyoshi Kaya-no-Miya, who died on Sept. 1st, 1932. Was at one time an aviation enthusiast for which the Prince was popular called "Prince of the Air" and established a private aviation institute (Mikuni Aviation School). — p. 45 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### The Imperial House — Other Members of the Imperial Family — Nashimoto-no-Miya

**Prince Morimasa** head and 2nd of the line, 4th son of the late Prince Asahiko; born March 9th, 1874. Field Marshal and Supreme War Councillor. Studied at a French Military School in 1903-04 and again in 1907-08; took part in the Russo-Japanese War (1904-05); after holding various high posts including the post of divisional commander was promoted to full General in 1923 and then appointed member of the Supreme War Council; Field Marshal, August, 1932. The Prince is Honorary President of the Franco-Japanese Society, the Japan Agricultural Association, the Japan Forestry Association, the Japan Martial Art Association, the Imperial Aero Association, the Italian Society of Japan etc. — p. 46 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Itsuko** consort of the above, 2nd daughter of the late Marquis Naotada Nabeshima; born Feb. 2nd, 1882; married Prince Morimasa Nov. 28th, 1900; made a tour of Europe with the Prince in 1908-09. — p. 46 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

### Royal House of Chosen

**Ri** the former royal family of Chosen (Korea). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Gin** head of the family and younger brother of Prince Chiok (the late head of the house), born October 20th, 1897 in Keijo (Seoul). Brought up in the royal palace in the former Korean capital but later moved to Tokyo to receive education. Graduated from the Military Academy in Tokyo in 1920; promoted to Captain and attached to the 2nd Infantry Regiment of the Imperial Guards Division in 1926; later attached to the General Staff Office; promoted to Lieut.-Colonel and attached to the Military Training Department; appointed Colonel and Commander of the 59th Infantry Regiment August, 1935, appointed head instructor of the preparatory course, Military Staff College, July, 1937 promoted to Major-Gen. July, 1938; married Princess Masako in 1920; visited Europe in 1927 for study and observation accompanied by Princess Masako. Residence in Tokyo—Kioi-cho. Kojimachi-ku). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Masako** consort of the above, eldest daughter of H.I.H. Prince Morimasa Nashimoto; born November 4th 1901; married Prince Gin in 1920. — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Im** consort of the late Prince Chiok Ri, born September 19th, 1894; widow in 1926, (Residence—Seoul, Chosen). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Ri Ken** eldest son of Prince Ri Kang, born October 28, 1909. Graduated at the Military Academy; is Captain of Cavalry. (Residence—Tokiwamatsu, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Yoshiko** consort of the above, eldest daughter of Mr. Hiroshi Matsudaira; born October 6th, 1911; married the Prince in October 1931. (Issue—Two sons). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Ri Ko** 5th son of the late Grand Prince Ri and father of Prince Ri Ken; born March 30th, 1877. — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Kin** consort of the above and eldest daughter of the late Baron Kin; born December 22nd, 1880; married December 6th, 1893. — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Prince Ri Gu** 2nd son of Prince Ri Kang; born November 15th, 1912. Graduated at the Military Cadet School and is now Captain of Artillery. — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

**Princess Sanshu** consort of the above and daughter of Marquis Boku; born December 11th, 1914; married May 3rd, 1935. Issue:—A son. (Residence—Tokiwamatsu, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo). — p. 47 ([scan part 1, leaf 96](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n96/mode/1up))

## Japan — Press and Publications: Leading Newspapers

### Leading Newspapers

**Chugai Shogyo Shimpo** (started in 1876). Economic and Commercial paper, issues both morning and evening editions, Pres., T. Tanaka; Ed., T. Obama. Office—Kayaba-cho, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Hochi Shimbun** (started in 1872). Issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., S. Noma; Ed., S. Okano. Office—Yurakucho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Jiji Shimpo** (started in 1882). Amalgamated into Tokyo Nichi Nichi in December, 1936. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Kokumin Shimbun** (started in 1892). Founded by Iichiro Tokutomi who retired in 1928; issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., M. Shiki; Ed., I. Yamanouchi. Office—Ginza-Nishi 7-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Miyako Shimbun** (started in 1885). Social paper, Pres., E. Fukuda, Ed., H. Watanabe. Office—Uchisaiwaicho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Asahi Shimbun** (started in 1888). Sister paper to the Osaka Asahi Shimbun; issues boht morning and evening editions. Pres., S. Uyeno; Ed., T. Ogata. Office—Yurakucho 2-chome Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Nichi-Nichi** (started in 1872). Sister paper to the Osaka Mainichi, issues both morning and evening editions. Chairman of Board M. Oka; Ed., S. Takaishi. Office—Yurakucho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))

**Yomiuri Shimbun** (started in 1874). Issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., M. Shoriki; Ed., U. Takahashi. Office—Ginza-Nishi 3-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 161 ([scan part 1, leaf 219](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n219/mode/1up))


## Japan — Press and Publications: Newspapers, English dailies and news agencies

### Leading Newspapers

**Kobe Yushin Nippo** (started in 1884). Rep., K. Nakai; Ed., T. Yamada. Office—Sakaecho, Kobe. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

**Hokuroku Times** (started in 1907). Issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., S. Tanaka; Ed., J. Shibuya. Office—Soguruwa, Toyama City. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

Office—Uchiyamashitacho, 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

**Japan Chronicle** (est. 1868). An English paper (former Kobe Chronicle incorporated with Hyogo News). Subscription (per annum)—Daily ¥38.00 at home and ¥59 abroad; Weekly ¥18.00 at home and ¥25.00 abroad. Ed., & Pub., E. A. Kennard, Bus. Mgr. S. Foley. Office—65 Naniwa-machi, Kobe. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

**Japan Times & Mail** (est. 1897). Founded by the late S. Yamada, Motosada Zumoto, late Yoshitaro Takenobu and others, as the then only English newspaper conducted and edited by Japanese; incorporated with the Japan Mail (started by the late Capt. Brinkley) in 1924. Subscription (per annum)—Daily ¥30.00 at home and ¥55.000 abroad. Pres., H. Ashida; Exec.-Ed. Yasotaro Morri. Office—Uchisaiwai-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

### News Agencies

**Domei Tsushinsha** (est. 1936) The Domei Tsushinsha was established by the co-operation of the leading newspapers and the Japan Broadcasting Association through the good offices of the Government and opened to business on January 1, 1936 using the Shimbun Rengo Tsushinsha as its nucleus. Subsequent negotiations with the Nippon Dempo induced it to participate in the Domei's news service. As a result, the Nippon Dempo's news service department, together with the domestic and overseas branches, joined the Domei on May 31. Almost all city and rural newspaper also joined it on the same day. Thus, the Domei has come to control 70 branches at home and abroad. At the same time its advertising department joined that of the Nippon Dempo. So the Domei and the Nippon Dempo are destined to co-operate closely, the former as the greatest news agency and the latter as the greatest advertising agency. Pres. Y. Iwanaga, Managing Dirs., T. Hatakeyama, I. Furuno, S. Uyeda, Y. Hori. — p. 165 ([scan part 1, leaf 220](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n220/mode/1up))

## Japan — Social Problems: Organs for control, deliberation and arbitration (private institutes)

**The Kyocho-kai** (Tokyo).—Organized in 1919 by the Government authorities, university professors, business men, social workers, etc., to effect the “harmonization of capital and labour.” — p. 209 ([scan part 1, leaf 264](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n264/mode/1up))

**Ohara Social Problems Research Institute** (Osaka).—Established in 1919 by Mr. Ohara, a millionaire in Okayama, it conducts all important researches on social problems in the country, the staff including Dr. Iwasaburo Takano (Chief) and a number of able experts. — p. 209 ([scan part 1, leaf 264](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n264/mode/1up))

**Kurashiki Institute for the Research of the Science of Labour** (Kurashiki, Okayama prefecture).—Also founded by Mr. Ohara. Investigates the scientific aspects of the labour problem. — p. 209 ([scan part 1, leaf 264](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n264/mode/1up))

**Industrial Labour Investigation Office** (Tokyo).—Established in 1924, chiefly by representatives of labour organizations and scholars, to investigate political, economic and social affairs of the country. — p. 209 ([scan part 1, leaf 264](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n264/mode/1up))

**Arima's Agrarian Research Institute** (Tokyo).—Established by Count R. Arima to devote itself to the study of agrarian problems, which are now growing in importance and attracting the serious attention of the public, in consequence of the wide awakening of the peasant class. — p. 209 ([scan part 1, leaf 264](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n264/mode/1up))


## Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Leading Shipowners (company notes)

### Leading Shipowners

**Nippon Yusen Kaisha (Japan Mail S.S. Co.)** Founded in October, 1885, the Nippon Yusen Kaisha, which is one of the two premier maritime companies of Japan, celebrated the jubilee in October, 1935. The company was established by the amalgamaion of two rival concerns, the Mitsubishi and the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha. By the amalgamation of the two companies the N. Y. K. inherited 29 steamers and 1 sailing vessel from the Mitsubishi Company and 29 steamers and 10 sailing crafts from the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha, making a total of 69 vessels. Of these the 58 steamers totalled 64,610 tons gross and the 11 sailing vessels 4,725 tons gross. Between Japan and New York the Company maintains what is one of the most up-to-date freight services on the oceans to-day. The company put into commission in the Jubilee Year six new motor vessels on its Orient-New York Express Service. These six sister ships are all of 9,000 tons and their speed 18½ knots. Three of them were built in Nagasaki and three in Yokohama. The company owns several motorships on its Pacific run. These are the Chichibu Maru (17,500 tons), the Asama Maru (17,000 tons) and the Tatsuta Maru (17,000 tons). These, along with the Taiyo Maru, run a fast fortnightly service from Hong-Kong to Los Angeles and San Francisco, via Honolulu. On the European run the company has also excellent boats, the Terukuni Maru and the Yasukuni Maru being the finest ships on the service. They are both of 11,900 tons gross. The following is a list of the important N.Y.K. passenger and freight services:— Japan-European Fortnightly Service; Orient-California Fortnightly Service; Japan-Australia Monthly Service; South American West Coast Monthly Service; Japan-Bombay Monthly Service; Japan-China Rapid Express Service. Besides the above the company maintains regular passenger services from Japan to Tsingtao, the South Sea Islands, Tientsin, Formosa, etc., the last two being operated by the N. Y. K. Line. The authorized capital of the company as in 1937 was ¥106,250,000, of which ¥78,250,000 was paid up. — p. 248 ([scan part 1, leaf 303](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n303/mode/1up))

**Osaka Shosen Kaisha (Osaka Mercantile S.S. Co.)** The Company was established in 1884 by the amalgamation of small shipping companies which had steamers plying between ports in the inland sea. The field of operation has subsequently been enlarged and it enjoys at present a commanding position in Japanese shipping. The following is a list of the important O. S. K. passenger and freight services:— South American Monthly Service; New York Rapid Express Monthly Service; East Coast African Monthly Service; Bombay Twice Monthly Service; Calcutta Twice Monthly Service; Australia Monthly Service; South Seas Service (South Seas Subsidized Service, South Seas Voluntary Service, Philippine Service, Saigon-Bangkok Service). The Company also maintains a regular passenger service from Japan to important places in Formosa, China, Korea, Dairen, etc. The authorized capital of the Company as in 1937 was ¥100,000,000, of which ¥62,500,000 is paid up. — p. 249 ([scan part 1, leaf 303](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n303/mode/1up))

## Manchoukuo — Education: Japanese educational institutions (leading institutions)

**Manchuria Medical University** Established at Mukden by the South Manchuria Railway in June, 1911 for Japanese and Manchurian students. Course: preparatory 3 yrs., university 4 yrs. Enrollment at the end of April, 1936—university course, 287; preparatory course and special preparatory course, 240; special course 137. Clinic attached. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Port Arthur Engineering University** Formerly Port Arthur Engineering School. Elevated to university status August, 1922. Departments: mechanical engineering, electric engineering, mining, metallurgy. Course: preparatory 3 yrs., university 4 yrs. Enrollment at the end of April, 1936: Preparatory course, 253; University course, 162. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Russso-Japanese Association School** Established, 1920 at Harbin by the Late Count Goto. Course, 3 yrs., Special course 1 yr. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**South Manchuria Technical College** Established at Dairen. Formerly, South Manchuria Technical School. Elevated to college status, 1922. Course, 3 yrs. Departments: architectural, mechanical. Enrollment in May, 1936: 276. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Industrial Training Schools** Established at Fushun and Penhsihu. Object: practical technical training. Course, 3 yrs. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Agricultural Training Schools** Established at Kungchuling and Hsingyaocheng. Course, 1 to 2 yrs. With dormitory facilities. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Commercial Training Schools** Established at Yingkow and Liaoyang in 1928. Course, 1 to 2 yrs. With dormitory facilities. — p. 685 ([scan part 1, leaf 744](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n744/mode/1up))

**Mukden Trade Association** The Mukden Trade Association was organized in December, 1912 by the Japanese traders resident at Mukden. The members of the association as in July, 1936 numbered 35. It handles chiefly wheat, flour, sugar, furs and hides, rubber shoes, textiles, toilet goods and others. It is steadily being carried on between Manchoukuan consumers and exporters in Japan. — p. 777 ([scan part 1, leaf 834](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n834/mode/1up))

## Who's Who

### A

**Aall, Cato N. B** Hon. Consul for Norway in Tokyo; Chairman of Board of Dirs. Aall & Co., Tokyo, Osaka and Kobe; b. Aug. 1865, Vadsö, Norway; s. of Rev. Nils Anthon Aall. Career: grad. Com. Academy, Oslo, Norway; Hon. Consul for Norway and Sweden in Johannesburg, Transvaal; was for many yrs. in France, England, Canary Islands, America, China and Belgium. Address: 426/7, Mitsubishi 21-gokan, Marunouchi 3-chome, Tokyo. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Genki 安倍源基** Metro. Police Chief since Dec., 1937; b. Feb. 14, 1894, Yamaguchi-ken; e. s. of Hanjiro Abe; m. Fujiko, e. d. of Masanosuke Akiyama. Career: grad. Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; served Okinawa, Kochi and Aichi Prefs.; Secr. Home Office; Chief Educ. Bur. of Yamagata-ken; Chief Spec. Higher Police Dept., Metro. Police Board, 1932; Police Chief of Home Office. Address: Metro. Police Board, Tokyo. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Isoh 安部磯雄** M.P.; Pres. Shakai Taishuto (Social Mass Party); Mem. Tokyo Muni. Assembly; b. Feb. 4, 1865, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Gonnojo Okamoto; adopted by Abe family. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ.; studied in Europe and America; joined Christian movement in Okayama City; Instructor Doshisha; Prof. Waseda Univ.; founder and Pres. Shakai Minshuto (Japan's first proletarian political party) 1926; when Shakai Minshuto and Rodo Taishuto were merged into the new Shakai Taishuto, July 1932, apptd. Pres. Address: 107 Yedogawa Apts., Ushigome-ku, Tokyo. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Jiro 阿部次郎** Prof. in Æsthetics at Tohoku Imp. Univ. since 1923; b. Aug. 1883, Yamagata-ken; s. of Tomitaro, teacher. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; Lecturer Keio Univ. 1913; same. Japan Women's Coll. 1917; despatched to Europe for study by Educ. Dept. 1922-23. Address: 245 Tsuchitoi, Sendai. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Kiichiro 阿部喜市郎** M.D.; Physician; b. Dec. 14, 1880, Gumma-ken; s. of late Sakutaro, mine operator. Career: studied Medical Science (especially Radiant Ray Remedy); studied in Germany, Austria and France 1923; on return home founded Abe Hospital and Cancer Research Institute. Address: 1 Maruyama Fukuyama-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Nobuyuki 阿部信行** General on the reserve list. See 1936 issue. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abe, Yoshimune 阿部義宗** Pres. Aoyama Gakuin; b. Dec. 3 1886, Hirosaki City. Career: grad. Aoyama Gakuin; Drew Theol. Seminary (B.D.); New York Univ. (M.A.); Chairman, Nat. Committee, Y.M.C.A. of Japan. Address: Aoyama Gakuin, Midorigaoka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 943 ([scan part 1, leaf 1004](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1004/mode/1up))

**Abo, Kiyokazu 安保清種** Baron; Admiral (Reserve); Mem. House of Peers; Advisory Councillor to Cabinet; b. Oct. 15, 1870, Saga-ken; s. of Tanetetsu Sawano; later adopted by late Baron Kiyoyasu Abo; m. Sueko. Career: grad. Nav. Acad.; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; Captain H.M.S. Akitsushima; Staff 2nd Fleet; Nav. Gen. Staff Bd.; Chief, Nav. Tech. Dept.; Comdr.-in-Chief Kure and Yokosuka Nav. **Adachi, Buntaro 足立文太郎** M.D.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; b. June 1865, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Chozo Adachi. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1894; studied Anat. & Anthrop. in Germany; Prof. 3rd Higher Sch.; Prof. and later Dean Med. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; resigned 1925; Pres. Osaka Higher Med. Sch. Cambridge; English Bar (Inner Temple) 1898; Fellow, Univ. Coll. Oxford 1895-1902; Whewell Scholar, Univ. of Cambridge 1893; Hon. Secr.-Gen. Int'l Law Assn. 1905-1916; organized conferences at Christiania, Berlin, Portland (Me.), Budapest, London, Paris and Madrid; Associate, Institut de Droit Int'l and Academie Diplomatique; former Examiner, Oxford, Liverpool, Manchester, London and Hongkong Univs.; was contributed an album of calligraphy by many notables on his 70th birthday 1938. **Bischoff, Ernest** Dr. Phil.; German Consul at Dairen since 1935; b. July 1880, Muenchen; s. of Theodor Bischoff, director of a railway company; m. Hertha Bischoff, née Zelle. Address: c/o German Consulate, Dairen. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Bleackley, Horace Vivian** Mng.-Dir. Sale & Co. Ltd., Tokyo; b. July 16, 1907, Walton-on-Thames, Surrey, England; s. of Horace William Bleackley; married. Career: grad. Radley Coll. 1926; studied in Paris 1926; served Sale & Co., London 1927, Hudson's Bay Co. 1929; with Sale & Co. Ltd., Tokyo since 1929. Address: 86 Harajuku 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Boku, Ei-ko 朴泳孝** Marquis (cr. 1910); Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Board of Councillors Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Pres. Keijo Spinning Co.; Dir. Chosen Land Improvement Co.; b. June 1861, Bannan, Suigen District, Keiki-do. Career: held important positions in political circles in Chosen since 1892; nominated Peer 1933. Address: 81 Suijin-do, Keijo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Boku, Ei-tetsu 朴榮喆** Mem. Board of Councillors, Chosen Govt.; Pres. Chosen Com. Bank since 1931; Spec. Mem. Keijo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Hon. Cons.-Gen. of Manchoukuo at Keijo; b. Feb. 1879, Zenshu; s. of Boku Ki-jun. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Gov. Kogendo and Kita-Kankyodo; Inspector, Oriental Development Co.; Pres. Sannan Bank 1927; Vice-President of present bank 1928; Pres. 1931. Address: 144 Shokakudo, Keijo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Boku, Shun-kin 朴春琴** Pres. Soai-kai; Mng.-Dir. Nissen Enterprise Co.; Prop. Nissen Kaikan; b. Apr. 1891, Keisho Nando, Chosen. Career: grad. Mitsuyo Kanbun Shojuku (Chinese Classics Sch.); Nichigo Gakko (Japanese Language Sch.); founded Sokyu-kai (Mutual Relief Society), Soai-kai (Mutual Friendship Society); went to Manchuria and Mongolia to inspect condition of Chosenese; sent to Diet from Tokyo 1932. Address: 1 Umayabashi, Honjo-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Bose, Rash Behari** Journalist; Lecturer; Corr. of Indian Papers; Editor of "New Asia," a monthly paper standing for Complete Independence of Asia; b. Mar. 1886, Bengal, India; n. Indian; Naturalized as Japanese citizen, 1923; s. of Benode Behari Bose, official. Career: grad. Dupleix Coll., French Chandernagore; Morton Inst., Calcutta, India; worked as Chief Clerk, Forest Research Institute, Indian Govt.; joined Indian Independence Agitation and led revolutionary movement in India 1910-15; was charged by the Indian Govt. with sedition, conspiracy to wage war against the British King, creating disaffection among Indian soldiers for revolutionary purposes, throwing bomb upon and severely injuring Lord Hardinge, Viceroy of India, and a reward of twelve thousand Rupees was announced for his arrest; fled from India as refugee after unsuccessful uprising in 1915 to Japan, where he was ordered to be deported by Japanese Govt., but rescued and protected by Mitsuru Toyama, late Premier Inukai and other Japanese political leaders, and naturalized as Japanese Citizen; is active in Japan for Indian Independence, Asiatic Renaissance and World Peace based on justice and love; built "Asia Lodge," dormitory for Indian and other South Asiatic students, at 401 Yodobashi-machi, Tokyo; published the following books (in Japanese); Prospect of Revolutionary Asia, pages 325; Indian Tales of Wits, pages 340; India in Revolution, pages 428; India in Bondage, pages 334; Indian Folk Tales, pages 272; Victory of Young Asia, pages 245; and Cry of India, pages 345. Address: 79 Onden 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Brauns, Erik** Mining Engr.; Dir. Gadelius & Co.; b. Apr. 20, 1893 at Oskarstrom, Sweden; s. of Wilhelm Brauns, Businessman; m. Margit Olsson. Career: grad. Royal Tech. Univ. of Stockholm, Sweden, 1916; after holding various posts in Sweden and England, joined Gadelius & Co., Ltd., Tokyo, 1920. Address: 16 Kitano-cho 2-chome, Kobe. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Briceno, Julio E** Consul-Gen. for Panama at Yokohama since 1931; b. Feb. 14, 1910, Panama City; s. of Alejandro Briceno, judge, public notary, diplomat; m. Beatrice Schnahenbeck 1931; profession journalist; consular official. Career: Reporter "Panama-America," "Diario de Panama," "Grafico" and "Accion Comual," 1928-31; served Immigration Dept. Panama, Foreign Office 1930; Secr. to Premier Vallarino 1931; Chief of 1st Sec., Dept. of Justice 1931; since Mar. 20, 1931 Consul at Yokohama. Address: Panama Consulate, 157 Yamashita-cho, Naka-ku, Yokohama. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Bruce, Robert Randolph** Hon. B. Sc., C.E., F.R.G.S., LL.D.; Canadian Min. to Tokyo since 1936; b. July 1863 at St. Andrew's, Lhanbryd. Elgin; s. of Rev. Charles Bruce, M.A.; m. 1st Lady Elizabeth Northcote (deceased), y. d. of 2nd Earl of Iddlesleigh; 2nd, Edith Badgley, d. of late W. A. Molson, M.D., widow of Richard Benedict Van Horne, 1932. Educ.: The Gymnasium old Aberdeen; Glasgow Univ. Career: Scientific Staff, Wm. Denny Bros. Dumbarton, 1883-87; went to Canada 1887; Eng. Staff, C. P. Railway, 1887-95; engaged in mining, British Columbia, 1897-1925; Pres. Mine Owners' Assn. of the Interior, 1923-25; Lieut.-Gov., British Columbia, 1926-31; Dir., Consolidated Mining & Smelting Co. of Canada. Address: Canadian Legation, 16 Omote-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Brumbaugh, Thoburn Taylor** Methodist Missionary; b. Aug. 1896, Agosta, Ohio; s. of Rev. E. G. Brumbaugh, Methodist Minister. Career: grad. Oberlin Business Coll. Ohio 1914; Army service, U. S. A. and in France 1917-1[?]; Ohio Wesleyan Univ. Delaware 1920 (B.A.); Sch. of Theol. Boston Univ. 1924 (S.T.B.); Union Theol. Sem. New York 1930 (S.T.M.); Methodist Student Pastor, Harvard Univ. 1923-24; Asst. Pastor, Grace Methodist Church, Dayton, Ohio 1922-23; Missionary in Japan since 1924. Publications: "Religious Values in Japanese Culture." Address: 65 Miyashita-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Bruner, Glen Willard** B.S.; M.A.; Attache of American Emb., Tokyo; b. Aug. 22, 1897, Red Cloud, Nebr., U. S. A.; s. of Chas. E. Bruner. Career: U.S. Reclamation Service 1917; U.S. Army 1917-19; taught Sci. at Eaton High Sch. 1919-20; educational work in Japan 1920-31; Amer. Vice-Cons. at Nagasaki 1931-37; Language Officer Amer. Emb. Tokyo 1937. Address: 6 Hinoki-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 950 ([scan part 1, leaf 1011](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1011/mode/1up))

**Buchanan, Daniel Crump** B.A.; M.A.; B.D.; Ph. D.; Missionary of Presbyterian Church in U.S.A.; engaged in Newspaper Evangelism; b. June 1892, Kobe; s. of Dr. William C. Buchanan, missionary for 44 years in Japan; m. Katharine Baetjer. Career: grad. Fredericksburg Coll. 1912; Washington and Lee Univs. 1914; Presb. Theol. Sem. Chicago 1921; Hartford Sem. Foundation 1934; taught in Hagi Middle Sch. Yamaguchi-ken 1914-16; Yamaguchi Middle Sch. and Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch. 1916-17; Kwansei Gakuin 1917-18; went to U.S. to join army as volunteer 1918; returned to Japan as ordained missionary 1921; joined Asiatic Society of Japan as life member 1921; published "Inari: Its Origin, Development, and Nature", 1935. Address: Ichijo-dori, Muro-machi Nishi, Kyoto. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Buncombe, William Pengelley** B.A. (Cambridge Univ. England); Missionary; b. June 1856, Taunton, Somerset, England; s. of William Buncombe, lawyer. Career: ordained in English Church 1883; Curate in Kingston-on-Thames and St. Paul's church for 5 yrs.; came to Japan as Missionary 1888. Address: 487 Asagaya 3-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Butler, Paul Dalrymple** H.B.M. Cons.-Gen. Mukden; b. Mar. 1886, Herriard, Hants, England; s. of Rev. G. H. Butler. Career: entered British Consular service 1908; served at Tokyo, Seoul, Tansui, Osaka, Manila, Yokohama. Address: British Consulate-Gen., Mukden. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

### C

**Cameron, Charles R** B.A.; American Cons.-Gen. at Tokyo; Phi Beta Kappa, Delta Chi; b. New York State, U. S. A. Career: grad. Cornell Univ. 1898; Philippine Civil Service 1901-17; Captain and Major U.S. Army 1917-19; Consul at Taona, Chile 1919-20, Pernambuco Brazil 1920-23, Tokyo 1923-25; Cons. and Cons.-Gen. at Sao Paulo Brazil 1927-34; Cons.-Gen. at Habana Cuba 1934-36, Osaka 1936-37; present post since 1937. Address: American Consulate-General, Tokyo. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Canali, Lionel** Major; Hon. Consul for Japan at Genoa and Turin; b. Mar. 1890, Genoa; s. of late Edward Canali. Address: Via Lomellini, 8, Genoa, Italy. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Catto, Alexander Ross** Cable Corr. & Ins. Agent since 1928; b. Oct. 1867, London; s. of John Catto; n. Scottish. Career: grad. St. Saviour's Coll. Ardingly; engaged in ins. business in London and various parts in the East; came to Japan first in 1893; returned to Japan 1902; joined J. Russell Kennedy 1927. Address: 13 Reinanzaka, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chamberlin, William Henry** A. B. (Haverford Coll.), Writer & Journalist; b. Feb. 1897, Brooklyn, New York; s. of Ernest V. Chamberlin; m. Sophie Trosten. Career: grad. William Penn. Charter Sch., Pa. 1913; Haverford Coll. Penn. 1917; connected with Philadelphia Press, Phila. Public Ledger, New York Tribune 1917-22; Staff Far Eastern Corr. of Same in Tokyo since Feb. 1935; Corr. of Christian Science Monitor at Moscow 1922-34; Author of "Soviet Russia" (1930)," "The Soviet Planned Economic Order" (1931); " Russian's Iron Age". (1934); "The Russian Revolution" (1935), etc. Address: 258 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chang Ching-hui 張景惠** General; Manchoukuo Prime Minister since 1935; b. 1871, Taian-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Fengtien; apptd. Major-Gen. 1916; Mil. Gov. of Chahar District and Comdr. 16th Div. 1920-22; Dir.-Gen. Nat. Highway Preparation Bureau 1924; War Min. in Ku Wei-chun Cabinet 1927; Min. of Ind. in Fan-Fu Cabinet; Gov.-Gen. Tung Sheng Spec. Dist.; Pres. Supreme War Council Nat. Govt.; joined Japanese Army for preservation of peace at Harbin at time of Manchurian Incident; Gov. Heilungkiang Prov. 1932; apptd. Pres. Privy Council and War Minister; concurrently Min. Dept. of Foreign Affairs; Dept. of Mongolia Adm., 1937. Address: Premier's Residence, Hsinking. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chang Hai-peng 張海鵬** General; Chief, Aide-de-Camp to Manchoukuo Emperor; Manchoukuo Privy Councillor; b. 1867 in Kaipin-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: apptd. Comdr. 55th Brig. of 28th Div.; Comdr. 4th North-East Cav. Div. and Tutelary Envoy in Taoliao 1927. Address: Manju Taigai, Hsinking. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chang I-san 張益三** See 1938 issue. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

Bureau; Magistrate Hailung-hsien Fengtien Prov.; Chief Chuangho Salt Fields; Councillor Fengtien Prov.; Chief Personnel Sec. of same 1932-35; Dir. Rites & Religions Bureaux 1935-37. Address: Dept. of People's Welfare, Hsinking. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

Address: Dept. of People's Welfare, Hsinking. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chang Shih-chao 章士釗** Chairman Judicial Yuan of Renovation Govt. of China; b. 1881, Hunan Prov., China; Career: grad. Edinburgh Univ. England; Pres. Peking Univ.; came to Japan as refugee after the 2nd revolution; returned China 1916; Prof. Peking Univ.; elected M.P.; delegate Shanghai Peace Conf. as Southern Repr. 1919; sent to Eur. and Amer. to inspect educ. condition 1919-22; Pres. State Agr. Coll. Peking 1922; later assisted in publishing business at Shanghai; Justice Min. under Tuan Chi-jui after the Feng Yu-hsiang's coup d'tat 1924; Educ. Min. 1925; Prof. Tungpeh Univ. Fengtien 1930; later opened law office at Shanghai; Mem. and Chief Secr. of Chicha (Hopeh-Chahar) Political Council 1936; present post upon establishment of Renovation Govt. of China Mar. 1938. Address: Nanking, China. — p. 951 ([scan part 1, leaf 1012](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1012/mode/1up))

**Chang, Shun-han 張書翰** Dir. Gen. Postal Admin. Bur. Manchoukuo since July 1938; b. 1891, Itung-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad. Pei-Yang Univ. Tientsin; Magistrate Changchun-hsien; Chief Yenki Muni. Adm. Planning Office; Supt. Yenki Marine Customs; Adviser Gov.'s Office, Kirin Prov.; Chief Educ. Dept. of Kirin 1934-36; Dir. Civil Affairs Bureau, Kirin Prov; Dir. Supervisory Bur. Home Office. Address: Home Office, Hsinking. — p. 952 ([scan part 1, leaf 1013](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1013/mode/1up))

**Chang Yen-ching 張燕卿** Vice-Chairman Hsinmin-Kai (Govt. Assn. of Public Welfare) of Provisional Govt. of China since Dec., 1937; b. Feb. 1898, Hopei Prov. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. Manchoukuo Boy Scouts; Privy Councillor of Man. Address: Hsinking. — p. 952 ([scan part 1, leaf 1013](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1013/mode/1up))

**Chang Wen-chu 張文鑄** Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 3rd Dist. Garrison (Tsitsihar) since 1932; b. 1898, Heilungkiang Prov. Career: grad. Paoting Mil. Acad.; Instructor Heilungkiang Mil. **Chapman, James Jeffries** D.D.; Clergyman; b. July 1873, Fauquier Country, Virginia, U. S. A.; s. of William Henry Chapman, Govt. official; m. Ellen Ritchie Scott. Career: missionary of Amer. Epis. Malmö Högre Almänna Läroverk; after 4 years' com, training in Hamburg, Germany, came to Japan and joined A. Meier & Co. 1896; Partner, same firm 1910-17; Swedish Vice-Consul, Yokohama 1906-16; Consul 1919; Dir. Winkel & Gedde, Ltd. Kobe & Yokohama 1918-22. **Gerede, R. Hüsrev** Turkish Ambassador to Japan since Mar. 1936; b. in Edirne, Turkey; s. of Gen. Mehmet dei Pasa. Career: started his career as Mem. General Staff Off. of Turkish Republic; is a close friend of Pres. Kāmal Atatürk; Mil. Attaché in Athens, later Comdr. in Balkan War and Great War; elected Rep.; apptd. Minister to Hungary 1924; stayed in London at the negotiation for peace as Turkish delegation of Nat. Govt. of Ankara for several times; Min. to Bulgaria 1926-30; to Iran 1930-34. Address: Turkish Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 959 ([scan part 1, leaf 1020](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1020/mode/1up))

Paris; Vice-Consul, Peking 1922-26; Consul, Keijo 1926-29; Vice-Consul, Shanghai 1930; Consul, Swatow 1930-31; Nanking, 1931-32; Asst. Consul, Tientsin 1932-35; First Chinese Secr. French Leg. Peking 1935; Consul Adjoint, Embassy, Peking 1935-36. Address: French Consulate, Mukden. — p. 959 ([scan part 1, leaf 1020](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1020/mode/1up))

**Godo, Takuo 伍堂卓雄** D.E.; Ordnance Vice-Admiral (retired); Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Nippon and Tokyo Chambers of Com. & Ind.; b. Sept. 1877, Kanazawa; s. of late Takuji Godo. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; entered naval service; Chief Ordnance Dept. Kure Naval Dockyard; Steel Mfg. Dept. of same; Ordnance Testing Dept.; Chief Aviation Dept. **Goedicke, Alfred E** Mgr. for Japan, Chemical Construction Corp.; b. 1879, Leoben, Austria; s. of Edward Goedicke, Steel Works Mgr. Career: grad. Address: 1733 Fukazawa-machi 4-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 959 ([scan part 1, leaf 1020](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1020/mode/1up))

**Goko, Kiyoshi 郷古潔** Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (merger of Mitsubishi Shipbldg. Co., Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. and Yokohama Dock Co.) since 1935; Dir. Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Dir. and Business Mgr. Mitsubishi Shipbldg. Co. 1928; Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. 1932. Address: 645 Yamanouchi, Kita-Kamakura, Ohfuna-machi, Kanagawa-ken. — p. 960 ([scan part 1, leaf 1021](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1021/mode/1up))

**Goto, Fumio 後藤文夫** Mem. House of Peers; b. Mar. 1884, Oita-ken; s. of late Yoshitomo Goto, official; m. Haru, sister of Viscount Hisaakira Kano. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. **Goto, Kunihiko 後藤國彦** Pres. Narita Ry. Co., Keisei Elec. Ry. Co.; b. July 2, 1891, Oita-ken; s. of Mitsuhiko Goto. Career: grad. Hosei Univ. 1911; joined Yomiuri Shimbun-sha; Chief, Econ. **Grew, Joseph Clark** Diplomat; American Amb. to Japan since 1932; A.B. (Harvard Univ. 1902); LL.D. (George Washington Univ. 1926); b. May 1880, Boston; s. of Edward Sturgis Grew. Career: grad. Groton Sch. 1898; Harvard Univ. 1902; travelled extensively in Europe & the East; Clerk in Cons.-General Cairo 1904; Vice-Consul Cairo 1904-06; 3rd Secr. Amer. Emb. Mexico City 1906-07; St. Petersburg 1907-08; 2nd Secr. Emb. Berlin 1908-11; Secr. Emb. Vienna 1911-12; Secr. Emb. Berlin 1912-16; Counsellor of same 1917; Counsellor Emb. and Chargé d'Affairs at time of break of diplomatic relations with Austria-Hungary Vienna 1917; assigned to Dept. of State Washington May 1917; Acting Chief Western Europe Affairs Div. Mar. 1918; attended Pre-Armistice Negotiations Versailles as Secr. Amer. Delegation Oct.- Nov. 1918; Secr.-Gen. Am. Commission to negotiate Peace with rank of E.E. & M.P. Paris Nov. 1918; assigned as Am. Secr. on Int'l Secretariat of Peace Conf. Jan. 1919; E.E. & M.P. to Denmark 1920; to Switzerland 1921; Am. Rep., Conference on Near Eastern Affairs Lausanne 1922-23; negotiated and signed Treaty with Turkey 1923; Am. Unofficial Rep. with Temporary Mixed Commn. of League of Nations for control of Traffic in Arms Geneva & Paris 1924; Under Secr. of State 1924-27; served as Chairman Personnel Examining and Sch. Boards of Foreign Service and as Mem. Central Comm. Am. Red Cross; Amb. to Turkey 1927-32. Address: American Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 960 ([scan part 1, leaf 1021](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1021/mode/1up))

**Gunji, Shigeru 郡司茂** Mgr. Hotel New Osaka since 1934; b. May 1897, Chiba-ken; s. of Fukutaro Gunji; m. Nobuko. Career: grad. Okura Higher Com. Sch.; joined The Imp. Address: 19 Imazu Urakaze, Nishinomiya City. — p. 960 ([scan part 1, leaf 1021](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1021/mode/1up))

Course; studied at Univs. of Leipzig and Vienna, 1902; medical practice at Inouye Ophthalmological Hospital; again studied at Univ. of Berlin and Leipzig 1909; Prof. Okayama Medical Coll.; Dir. Okayama Ophthal. Hospital, 1912; rec'd deg. 1914. Address: 66 Nagata-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**Inouye, Saburo 井上三郎** Marquis; Mem. House of Peers; Major-Gen. (retired); b. Feb. 6, 1887, Tokyo; s. of late Prince Taro Katsura, later adopted by late Marquis Katsunosuke Inouye. Career: grad. Mil. Acad.; studied in Europe and America 3 yrs.; Artillery Sub.-Lieut. 1906; Col. 1929; Chief Mobilization Sec. War Office. Address: 42 Miyamura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**Inouye, Shu 井上周** Pres. Koshien Hotel, Sanyo Chuo Hydro-Elec. Co., Nippon Simple Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Hanshin Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co., Keihan Elec. Ry. Co., Hanshin Kyuko Bus Co., Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; b. Apr. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Yasujiro Inouye, businessman. Career: grad. Antwerp Com. Coll. Belgium 1902; founded Toyo Paper Mills 1906; Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co. when the aforementioned firm was merged 1924. Address: 32 Naka 2-chome, Tezukayama, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**Inouye, Shukichi 井上周吉** Aud. Yoda Machine Ind. Co.; Dir. of several other cos.; b. Nov. 1881, Shiga-ken; s. of late Goemon Inouye; m. Haru, d. of Jisaburo Hirata, 1912. Career: studied Elec. Engrg. at Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Pres. Omishima Elec. Co. 1920; Pres. Yoshizaki Ry. Co. 1925-26; Pres. Hachioji Paper Mfg. Co. since 1931, Toa Commercial Co. 1934, Jochushi Seizo K. K. 1935. Address: Ibaraki-cho, Osaka-fu. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

Minister 1926-27. Address: 28 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

Univ.; Prof.; Dean Litt. Coll. Address: 109 Omote-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**Inouye, Tsugimatsu 井上繼松** See 1937 issue. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1035/mode/1up))

Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; Lecturer, Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer and Dir. Hosei Univ.; Lecturer, Keio, Meiji and Senshu Univ.; Pres. Tokyo Bar Assn. Address: 12 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1035/mode/1up))

Address: 53 Takanawa-Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**Isaka, Toyomitsu 井坂豊光** M.P.; Lawyer; b. Dec. 1881, Osaka; s. of Koki Isaka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1910; returned to Diet 5 times; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1934-36. **Ishibashi, Shojiro 石橋正二郎** Pres. Nihon Tabi K. K. and Bridgestone Tyre Co.; b. Feb. 1889, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tokujiro Ishibashi. Career: founded Nihon Tabi K. **Ishida, Kaoru 石田馨** See 1938 issue. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**Ishida, Taro 石田太郎** Pres. Sanyo Elec. Ry. Co. since 1934; Dir. Sinki and Sin-mei Motorcar Cos.; b. Oct. 1877; s. of Yasushige; m. Uta. Career: joined San-yo Ry. Address: 625 Kitasenzoku-cho, Omori-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Onoe, Kikugoro 尾上菊五郎** (See Terashima Kozo). — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Onozuka, Kiheiji 小野塚喜平次** D.L; Mem. House of Peers; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Academy; b. Dec. 21, 1870, Niigata-ken; s. of Heikichi Onozuka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. University 1895; went to Europe and America for study; apptd. Dean, Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. of same, 1928-34; rec'd deg. 1902. Address: 36 Kobinatadai-machi 2-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Osaki, Shinkichi 大崎新吉** Mng.-Dir. Okura & Co. (Mining) Ltd.; b. Mar. 1888 in Osaka-fu; s. of Komakichi Osaki, merchant; m. Chiyoko, d. of Kataro Ishikura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. **Osame, Sanji 納三治** M.E.; Pres. Akebono Brake Band Mfg. Co., Takata Tokyo; b. Dec. 19, 1873, Okayama-ken; s. of Hisayoshi Osame. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ., Cornell Univ., Ithaca, N.Y.; Engr. Co.; the latter Co. is the sole suppliers of this product to the Japanese Army and to domestic Automobile Manufacturers. Address: 666 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Oseko, Yukio 大迫幸男** Dep. Mayor of Harbin; b. Feb. 14, 1901, Kagoshima-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined S. M. R. Co. 1925; apptd. Commr. Gen. Affairs Board Manchoukuo State Council 1932; Councillor Manchoukuo Legation Tokyo; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. State Highways Bureau 1933-36; Councillor Hsingan North Prov. 1936-37. Address: Muni. Office, Harbin. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Oshima, Kenzo 大島堅造** Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Bank since 1932; b. Jan. 1887, Gunma-ken; s. of Naosaku Oshima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; entered present Bank; Vice-Chief, New York Branch; Chief, Foreign Dept. Head Office 1922; Mgr. 1925. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; Dir. Tokyo City Educ. Bureau; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Vice-Pres. World Fed. of Educ. Assns. Address: 52 Komagome Sendagi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Oshima, Rikutaro 大島陸太郎** (See 1938 issue). — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Oshima, Yoshikiyo 大島義清** D.E.; Dir. Teikoku Fuel Ind. Co.; b. Sept. 7, 1882, Hyogo-ken; s. of Shoji Kurosawa, and later adopted by Rokuro Oshima. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; went to America to study Applied Chem. 1915; toured Europe and America 1922; attended World Coal Conf. 1926, World Power Conf. Berlin 1930, same Wash. 1936; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 52 Jodoji Nishida-machi, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

Address: 57 Shimo-Takanawa-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Ota, Hanroku 太田半六** Pres. Teikoku Explosives Ind. Co., Tsurumi Gas Co.; Dir. Tokyo Gas Co.; b. Sept. 1874, Chiba-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Senmon Gakko (present Waseda Univ.) 1894; entered business since 1899. Address: 5 Fujimi-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Ota, Masataka 太田正孝** D. Econ.; M.P.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Finance; b. Nov. 1886, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Mankichi Ota. Career: grad. Econ. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; joined Hochi Shimbun, 1919; apptd. **Ota, Mitsuhiro 太田光凞** Pres. Nara Express Motor Transport Co.; Chairman Keihan Elec. Ry. Co., Hanwa Elec. Ry. Co., Daido Elec. Power Co.; b. Oct. 1874, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Kageaki Ota. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; entered Ry. Dept ; resigned and entered business. Address: 1618 Tomoroki-mura, Kita-Kawachi-gun, Osaka-fu. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Ota, Tamekichi 太田為吉** See 1936 issue. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Otaguro, Jugoro 太田黒重五郎** Dir. Kyushu Hydro-Elec. Co., Chuo Elec. Co., Electro-Chem. Ind. Co ; Adviser Kyushu Elec. Ry. Co.; b. June 1866, Shizuoka-ken; 2nd s. of Tatsuo Komaki; later adopted by Korenobu Otaguro. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; Mgr. Osaka Com. Museum; entered Mitsui Bussan Kaisha 1894; Mng.-Dir. Shibaura Engrg. Works. Address: 22 Higashiogi-machi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Otaka, Shojiro 大鷹正次郎** Min. to Latvia since 1938; b. Feb. 1892, Tokyo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered For. Office 1918; served Belgium; Eleve-Cons. at Harbin 1919 [illegible] Tientsin Aug. 1919; 3rd Emb. Secr. 1921; 3rd. Secr. to Leg. in Austria 1924; 2nd Secr. to Leg. in Netherlands 1926; Delegate Conf. on German Reparation Questions at Hungary 1929; 1st Leg. Secr. 1930; 1st Secr. to Emb. in Belgium 1933; Cons.-Gen. at Tsingtao. Address: Japanese Legation, Riga, Latvia. — p. 1023 ([scan part 1, leaf 1084](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1084/mode/1up))

**Otani, Kocho 大谷光暢** Count; Chief Abbot Otani Denomination of Shin Sect; b. Oct. 1, 1903, Kyoto; s. of Koen Otani; m. Satoko, 3rd d. of H. I. H. late Prince Kuniyoshi Kuni-no-miya, 1924. Career: grad. Otani Buddhism Univ. 1925; Chief Abbot Otani Denomination since 1925; succeeded peerage 1925; made culture tour of Manchuria and North China 1934; travelled throughout the country for enlightment 1936-37; consoled the Japanese forces in North and Central China 1938. Address: Shichijo-agaru, Karasumaru-dori, Shimokyo-ku, Kyoto. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Otani, Kozui 大谷光瑞** Farmer; b. Dec. 1876, Kyoto; s. of Koson Otani, priest; once married but his wife passed in Jan. 1911. Address: Yokujitsuso, Shusuishi, Dairen-shigai. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Otani, Sonyu 太谷尊由** Pres. North China Develop. Co. since June 1938; Mem. House of Peers; b. Aug. 1886, Kyoto; s. of late Count Koson Otani; m. Yasuko, d. of Viscount Hidenobu Koide. Career: elected Peer 1931; Minister of Overseas Affairs; sent to North Manchuria to inspect Immigration 1938. Address: 57 Myogadani, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Otani, Takejiro 大谷竹次郎** Pres. Shochiku K. K. (theatrical & cinema); b. Dec. 13, 1877, Kyoto; s. of Eikichi Otani. Career: Adviser Kabuki-za; Business Mgr. same; Pres. same; established Shochiku Theatrical Co. 1929. Address: 23 Nakarokuban-cho. Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Otsu, Toshio 大津敏男** Dir.-Gen. Kwantung Bur. since Mar. 1938; b. 1893, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. German Law Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; Commr. Home Dept.; Chief Police Affairs Dept. Fukuoka-ken 1931; Metro. Police Bd. 1932; Chief Home Dept. Nagasaki-ken 1932-34; Chief Econ. Dept. Kanagawa-ken 1935; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Civil Affairs Dept. 1926-37; Dir.-Gen. Manchoukuo Home Office 1937-38; Gov. Kwantung Prov. 1938. Address: Kwantung Bureau, Hsinking. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Ott, Eugen** Major-Gen. (retired); German Amb. in Tokyo since May 1938; b. Apr. 8, 1889, Rottenburg, Wuerttemberg, Germany; s. of Ott, Dist.-Gov. Career: entered army service after leaving sch.; Lieut. 1909; served in the World War 1914-18; entered Gen.-Staff 1917; after the War served in the Reichswehr-Min. and in the Front, was in 1933 sent to the Japanese Army, 111 Art. Reg. Nagoya; recalled to Germany 1936; promoted Mil Attache in Tokyo 1936; Major-Gen. 1937. Address: German Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Owada, Teiji 大和田悌二** Pres. Elec. Power Control Preparation Bur. of Communications Dept. since May 1938; b. Nov. 23, 1888, Oita-ken; 2nd s. of Kokichi Kaminohata; adopted s. of Kyubei Owada of Fukui-ken; married. Career: grad. Eng. Law Course Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1915; practised law 1915; entered Communications Dept. 1917; Instructor Nautical Sch.; Sec. Chief Mercantile Marine Bur. Com. Dept.; Chief Archives & Documents Sec. Com. Min.'s Secretariate; Chief Secr. same; Dir. Nagoya Com. Bur. 1934; Dir. Elec. Bur. Com. Dept. Address: c/o Communications Dept., Tokyo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Oxford, James Samuel** B. Litt.; LL. D.; Teacher; b. Jan. 1880, Louisiana, U.S.A.; s. of Samuel Smith Oxford. Career: grad. Daniel Baker Coll. Brownwood, Texas; Eastman Sch. of Com.; taught at Alma Mater 3 years, Inst. Ingles, Santiago, Chile, 2 years; Palmore Inst. Kobe, 25 years. Address: Palmore Institute, 28 Kitanagasa-dori 4-chome, Kobe. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Oyaizu, Shozo 小柳津正藏** Lieut.-Gen. (retired); Dir. Showa Steel Works; Chief Motive Power Dept. and Laboratory of same; b. May 24, 1881, Chiba-ken; married. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1901, Experimental Physics Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Mem. War Supply Committee of the Allies at London during the World War; Attache of Mil. Tech. Dept. in U S.A.; Dir. Tokyo and later Osaka Arsenals; resigned acting service and joined Showa Steel Works 1933. Address: 4, Naka-Dai-machi, Anshan, Manchoukuo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Oyama, Kuranosuke 小山倉之助** M.P.; b. Mar. 21, 1883; 2nd s. of Chobei Oyama; married. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Aud. Nippon Gyosei Gakkai (Local Admin. Soc.); Aud. Address: 219 Minami Shinagawa 1-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Ozaki, Motojiro 尾崎元次郎** Mayor of Shizuoka since 1935; b. Sept. 1870, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Ihei Ozaki. Career: grad. Shizuoka Middle Sch.; promoted to Captain in Mil. **Ozaki, Yukio 尾崎行雄** M.P.; b. Nov. 20, 1859, Miye-ken; s. of Yukimasa Ozaki, samurai. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Editor Yubin Hochi Shimbun, Niigata Shimbun; Commr. Statistics Bureau; sent to Diet from Miye-ken 20 times since 1890; Councillor Foreign Office; Minister of Educ.; Minister of Justice; Mayor of Tokyo; made inspection tour of Europe after World War 1919; again went to Europe & America 1931-33. Address: 1774 Hiro, Zushi-machi, Kanagawa-ken. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

Chief, Planning Dept. 1930; Chief, Harbour Sec. 1931. Address: 11 Hokeido, Seishin, Chosen. — p. 1024 ([scan part 1, leaf 1085](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1085/mode/1up))

**Ozone, Takematsu 小曾根貞松** Repr. Partner Hon-Ozone G. K.; Pres. Hanshin Iron Works, Kobe Gas Co., Amagasaki Gas Co., Tokiwa Ply Wood Co. Ltd.; Dir. Sanyo Hide & Leather Mfg. Bur.; Chief of Court Marshal; Advisory Councillor to State Council; Higher Staff to Comdr. Sung Che-yuan's Pingtsin Guards; Dir. Admin. Bur. of Chi-cha (Hopei-Charhar), 1936. Address: Tientsin Muni. **Pansing, Paul** Hon. Vice-Consul for Finland at Dairen; Merchant; b. Dec. 1888, Germany. Address: 212 Yamagata-dori, Dairen. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Pao Kang 葆康** Vice-Pres. Ind. Bank of Manchou since July 1938; b. Sept. 1882, Fengtien Prov.; s. of Pao Fu-jun. Career: grad. Mukden Mil. Acad. 1914; served Mukden Mil. Gov.'s Office; Chief Mil. Address: Ind. Bank of Manchou, Hsinking. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Pao Ming-chien 鮑明鈐** Ph. D.; Noted Scholar on Oriental Polit.; Prof. Kienkuo Univ. of Manchoukuo since Apr. 1938; b. 1894 Chekiang Prov., China. Career: grad. Chinghua Univ. of Peking; further studied at Yale, Columbia and Johns Hopkins Univ., U.S.A.; entered educ. works in China; Dean Eng. Faculty at Peking Higher Normal Sch.; Reporter Peking Nippo (English edition) Pub. Co.; delegated to Pacific Sci. Conf., Honolulu, 1927; Prof. Peking State Univ. and Lecturer Peking Girls' Normal Sch.; came to Japan as Secr. to Chen You-jen 1931. Publications: International Relations of China, The Open-door Policy (English), etc. Address: Kienkuo Univ., Hsinking. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Paravicini, Fritz** M.D.; Medical Practitioner; b. 1874, Ennenda, Glarus, Switzerland; n. Swiss; s. of Emil Paravicini, physician. Career: studied at Swiss Schools and Univ.; after receiving degrees in Switzerland, served as Asst. and Locumtenens at Univ.-Clinics and Hospitals of Basle, Berne, Zurich, Engadine, and German hospitals, London; P.-G. work in Germany, France, U.S.A.; in charge of Sanatorium near Zurich; practised in Switzerland and Milan; in Yokohama and Tokyo since 1905; Med. Officer to Brit. Emb. Tokyo 1921-28; visited prisoners' camps on behalf of Int'l Red Cross Committee during World War; delegate of same Committee at Red Cross Conf. 1926, 1934 and 1937 in Tokyo; Swiss Del. at World Educ. Conf. Tokyo 1937. Address: 772 Honmoku 3-chome, Yokohama. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Pasquet, Maurice** American Vice-Consul at Dairen since 1937; b. July 1902, Newport, Rhode Island, U. S. A.; s. of Pierre Paul Pasquet; m. Suzanne Rambaut. Career: American Consulate General, Paris, 1925-31; Vice-Consul, Paris, 1931-34; Glasgow, Scotland, 1934-37. Address: 35 Yanagi-machi, Dairen. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Pearce, Reginald Worth** Danish Consul at Kobe & Osaka; b. 1876, Stourbridge, Worcestershire, England; s. of Horace Pearce, merchant. Career: grad. Hereford Coll. Herefordshire England; Fruit Farming in California 1894-98; served in Sale & Co. Yokohama 1899-1908; engaged in trade as Pres. Pearce & Co. Yokohama 1908; removed to Kobe 1923; Danish Consul 1929. Address: (home) 66 Kitanocho 4-chome, Kobe. (Office) 92 Yedo-machi, Kobe. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Perkins, P. D** M.A. (Univ. of Southern Calif.); Bibliographer & Prof. of English; b. Jan. 1897, Windsor, Vermont, U.S.A.; s. of Karl W. Perkins; m. Ione Bendel. Career: for 15 years, business executive; Prof. of English Daisan Koto Gakko since 1935; Co-founder and first research fellow of "Soc. for Oriental Studies" of Los Angeles, Calif. Author of "Lafcadio Hearn: A Bibliography of His Writings," 1934. Address: Sanko Kansha, Kyoto. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Phipps, Gerald Hastings** H. B. M. Cons.-Gen. Keijo Korea since Dec. 1934; b. June 1882; s. of Eccleston A. E. Phipps; m. Aline M. Purvis. Career: apptd. Student Interpreter in Japan Oct. 1903; H. Consulate-General Keijo Chosen. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Piggott, Francis Stewart Gilderoy** Major-General; C.B., D.S.O.; British Military Attache in Tokyo 1921-26 and since 1936; b. Mar. 1883 in London; s. of Sir Francis T. Piggott, barrister-at-law; one time legal adviser to Prime Minister Ito of Japan 1888-91; later attorney-gen. of Mauritius; chief justice of Hongkong; m. Jane Smith. Career: educ. at Cheltenham Coll., Royal Military Acad., Woolwich; Captain 1911; Major 1916; Colonel 1923; Major-Gen. 1935; served in Great War; General Staff, War Office London 1914. 1920-21, 1927-30; Deputy Mil. Secr. to Secr. of War 1930-35. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Pinto, J. A. Abranches** Prof. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; Hon. Consul for Portugal at Tokyo; b. Nov. 1893, Cabanas. Conselho do Carregal do Sal. Portugal; s. of F. do Nascimento Pinto, army officer; m. Tsurue (Japanese). Career: Instituto Superior de Agronomia de Lisboa. Address: 32 Honcho-dori 5-chome. Nakano-ku. Tokyo. — p. 1025 ([scan part 1, leaf 1086](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1086/mode/1up))

**Preibisch, Werner** Dr. phil et dipl. ès Lettres; Prof. Lecturer of Yamaguchi Higher Sch. & Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch.; b. Nov. 1896, Ohlau, Germany; s. of Prof. Dr. Karl Preibisch. Career: graduate of Magdeburg Coll.; Captain of German Army 1914-19; studied Philosophy, German Literature and Roman Philology at Halle and Muenster, Siena (Italy), Sevilla (Spain), Paris et Besancon (France); Governor of Princes of Hessia; Prof. of High Schools; German Coll. at Athens (Greece). **Suzuki, Umetaro 鈴木梅太郎** D. Agr.; Pres. Inst. of Scientific Research of Manchoukuo; b. Apr. 7, 1874, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Shozo Suzuki, landowner. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Address: 42-B Yamate, Yokohama. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1102](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1102/mode/1up))

**Syme, David York** Hon. Consul for Japan at Melbourne, Australia; granted spec. audience by H. I. J. Majesty in Oct. 1937; awarded Imp. Order of Sacred Treasure (4th class); Shipowner; b. 1876, Melbourne; s. of late David York Syme, shipowner; m. Jessie Mary Laycock, d. of Burdett Laycock. Address: 31 King Street, Melbourne, Australia. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1102](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1102/mode/1up))

**Thurnheer, Walter** Swiss Minister to Japan; b. in Baden, Switzerland. Address: 1 Shimoniban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1049 ([scan part 1, leaf 1110](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1110/mode/1up))

**Thiebaut, Paul** Chief De Bataillon D'Infanterie Coloniale Brevete; Attache Militaire A L'Ambassade De France Au Japon; Address: French Embassy, 12 Shinryudo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1049 ([scan part 1, leaf 1110](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1110/mode/1up))

Address: Gov.'s Residence, Tunghua. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))
