Address: Manchuria Electric Co., Hsinking. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))

**Tinge, W. S. Y. 丁士源** General; Auditor Central Bank of Manchou since 1935; Adv. Manchuria Ind. Develop. Corp.; Ex-Minister of Manchoukuo to Japan; b. 1876, Wu Hsien, Chekiang, China. Career: studied at Tientsin Nav. Sch. 1893-96; joined Imp. Army commanded by Marshal Baron Sun Chin 1897-1901; studied at Lincoln's Inn London 1901-4; returned to Peking 1904 and organized 4th & 6th Divs. with Marshal Ma Yu-kun and Tuan Chi-jui; Dept. Chief Imp. Army Council 1905-7; attended 2nd Hague Conf. as Chinese Imp. Mil. Delegate 1907-8; Life Mem. Royal Geog. Soc. London 1907; Judge Advocate Gen. Imp. Chi. Army & Navy 1907-11; Dir. Gen. Metro. Police & Gendarmerie Training Quarters 1908-11; Sup't. Customs Hankow 1912-16; Mng.-Dir. Peking-Suiyuan Ry. 1916-20; Mem. Defence Committee 1916-20; A.D.C. personal to the President of China 1917-20; Mng.-Dir. Peking-Hankow Rys. 1918-20; Chief Aviation Dept. 1918-20; Mil. Mission to Siberia 1919-20; Dir.-Gen. Lung-yen Iron Mining Co. 1916-20; Editor Tientsin Daily News 1922-24; Vice-Chairman Fin. Readjustment Commn. 1924-27; Chairman Domestic Loan Service 1924-29; Dir. Sino-Franco Bank and Exchange Bank of China 1926-30; Manchoukuo Chief Executive's personal rep. in Europe 1932-23; Manchoukuo Min. to Japan 1933-35. Publications: World Navy 1909; Notes & Comments to the Rules and Regulations of War on Land 1911 etc. Decorations: Chevalier Legion d'Honneur 1906; 5th Order of Merit, Republic of China 1920; 2nd Class Excellent Corps 1914; 2nd Class, Civil Tiger, 1915; 2nd Class Presious Excellent Corps 1917; 2nd Order of Merit, Manchou Tikuo 1934; 2nd O. M. Japanese Empire; 2nd Order of S Gregorii Magni, Vaticana, 1936. Address: (office) c/o Central Bank of Manchou, Hsinking. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))

Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1918; Lecturer Alma Mater 1919; Asst. Prof. same 1921; granted deg. 1925; studied abroad 1928-30; Prof. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1930; Chief Botanical Garden since 1936. Address: Bot. Garden Residence, Nishi 10-chome, Kita 2-jo, Sapporo. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))

**Togo, Minoru 東鄕實** D. Agr.; M.P.; b. Nov. 12, 1881, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Sanehiko Togo, farmer. Career: grad. Sapporo Agr. Councillor of Communications; Parl. Vice-Minister of Educ. 1932-34. Address: 8 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))

**Togo, Shigenori 東鄕茂德** Ambassador to U.S.S.R. since October 1938; b. Dec. 1882, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Toshikazu Togo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Eleve-Consul Mukden; 3rd Secr. Legation, Switzerland; 2nd Secr., Embassy, Berlin; Chief, 1st Sec., America & Europe Bureau, Foreign Office; 1st Secr. Embassy, Washington 1925; Councillor, Embassy Berlin; Dir. Europe & Asia Bur. House of Peers since 1911; Mem. Imp. Govt. Tariff Committee, Dumping Committee, Text Book Committee; Pres. Japan Wireless Telegraph Co. **Tohyama, Ikuzo 遠山郁三** M.D (1914); Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; b. Mar. 1877, Gifu-ken; s. of Doei Tohyama, physician. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; studied Dermatology at P. G. Course; Prof. Sendai Med. Coll. 1907; studied in Europe & America 1917; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1918; despatched to Europe & America 1935; Dir. Rikkyo Univ. 1937. **Toki, Akira 土岐章** Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 18, 1892, Tokyo-fu; s. of Viscount Yoritomo Toki; adopted by Yoritoshi Toki. Career: studied at Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. **Tokugawa, Iyemasa 德川家正** See 1938 issue. — p. 1050 ([scan part 1, leaf 1111](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1111/mode/1up))

**Tokugawa, Iyesato 德川家達** Prince (cr. 1884); Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Japan Red Cross Soc., Saiseikai (Imp. Gift Charitable Foundation); b. **Tomabechi, Gizo 苫米地義三** Pres. Shinko Colliery Co.; Sr. Mng.-Dir. Sulphuric Ammonium Sales Co.; Vice-Pres. Hachinohe Bank; Dir. Dai Nippon Oils & Fats Co.; Aud. Nippon Sulphar Co.; b. Address: Gov.'s Residence, Heiho. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Wang Tzu-hui 王子惠** Ind. Min. Admin. Yuan of Renovation Govt. of China; b. 1892, Amoy, China. Career: grad. Political Course Waseda Univ., Japan; entered journalism and later Chinese Govt. service; Vice-Comdr. 2nd Div. of Revolutionary Army; Chief Staff Nat. Govt. of China; Mem. China-Japan Econ. Res. Committee; present post upon establishment of Renovation Govt. of China Mar. 1938. Address: Nanking, China. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Wang Yin-tai 王蔭泰** Industrial Minister Renovation Govt. of China since Apr. 1938; b. 1886, Chekiang Prov. Career: grad. 1st Higher Sch. of Japan 1906; Law Coll. Berlin Univ. Germany 1912; entered Peking Govt. service; Councillor Legislative Bur. of same 1913; Lecturer Peking Univ. 1913; came to Japan as spec. envoy 1917; Adv. to Chang Tso-lin at Fengtien 1921; Vice For. Min. under Tu Hsi-kuei Cabinet after the failure of Tuan's Cabinet; For. Min. under Pan-fu Cabinet 1927; Justice Min. of same 1928; returned to Fengtien upon evacuation of Fengtien Clique from Peking; later stayed in Shanghai and opened law office. Address: Industrial Dept., Nanking, China. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Wang Yun-hsiang 王允卿** Supt. Gen. Affairs Bd. Manchoukuo since 1938; b. 1890, Haicheng-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad Meiji Univ. Tokyo; Chief Prison Sec. High Procurator's Office Shansi Prov.; Prof. Shansi Univ.; Procurator Tientsin Local Procurator's Office; Vice-Chairman Registration Investigation Commn. 1932; Dir. Prison Bureau Justice Dept. 1933-37; Dir. Civil Affairs & Educ. Bureau Fengtien Prov.; Dir. Supervisory Bur. Home Office 1938 Address: c/o Gen. Affairs Bd., Hsinking. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Washio, Senzo 鷲尾[?]三** Mng.-Dir. Nippon Seimo Kogyo Co., Godo Keori K. K.; b. Dec. 1891, Hyogo-ken; s. of Mansuke Washio, sake brewer; m. Sue 1919. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1916; immediately joined Muslin Spinning & Weaving Co.; then joined Godo Keori Co.; went to Europe and America to inspect cotton industries 1922; director of Pacific Trading Co., Shirahama Hot Spring Hotel, etc. Address: 289 Kitabatake, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Washio, Shogoro 鷲尾正五郎** Ph. D.; Writer; b. Feb. 1883, Sumoto, Hyogo-ken; s. of Gensaku Washio; married. Career: studied phil. Address: 33 Nishi-Takaido 2-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1058 ([scan part 1, leaf 1119](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1119/mode/1up))

**Watanabe, Yoshio 渡邊義郎** Pres. Chuo Trust Co., Aichi Bank; Dir. Okuma Iron Works; b. Sept. 24, 1872, Aichi-ken; s. of Jin-emon Watanabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. **Wohlers, H** Merchant; b. Oct. 1898, Hamburg, Germany; m. Liesel Krueger; n. German. Address: c/o Bergmann & Co., Hachiman-dori 3-chome, Kobe. — p. 1059 ([scan part 1, leaf 1120](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1939/page/n1120/mode/1up))

**Woodd, Frederick Hampden Basil** M.A. (Cambridge Univ.); Missionary, Priest of Nippon Seikokwai; b. Mar. 1906. Osaka; s. of Rev. Charles Hampden Basil Woodd; m. Emily Hornby Foss. 1936.
